headline: Healey Promises NEW AGE 🏭 of INDUSTRIALISATION 🔥 for UK 🇬🇧
text:
CHANCELLOR 🧾 John HEALEY 🧔 is about to DROP 💥 a FAT 🍖 promise of a "new age of industrialisation" 🏗️ when he climbs on stage 🎤 at Labour's annual conference 🏟️ in Liverpool on Monday ⏰!! This dude who used to be defence secretary 🛡️ will tell the delegates 🗣️ our coal mines ⛏️ are NOT coming back 🚫 but Labour is gonna remake Britain's industrial past 🏭 for the modern age by backing advanced manufacturing 🤖 with some serious legiSLAYtion 💼 that gets everyone edging 🫦 toward growth 📈 while he builds that new confidence in Britain 🇬🇧 like a total daddy 🍆 of the shipyards!! With just a month away from his first Budget 💰 the man is under massive pressure 🥵 to cut spending ✂️ or raise taxes 📈 to tackle that ballooning cost of government borrowing 📉 but he ain't spilling any Budget tea ☕ in this speech instead he's painting a positive vision 🌟 for British industry that will have the whole room throbbing 💓 with excitement over reindustrialisation!!

Healey will straight up ANNOUNCE 📢 plans to BOOST 🚀 Britain's shipbuilding industry 🛳️ with fresh orders for Royal Navy floating docks ⚓ and a shiny new maritime research vessel 🔬 that are gonna get built right here in the UK 🏴󠁧󁢁󁢁 instead of being shipped off to international tender 🌍!! Those three new floating docks at HM Royal Naval Base Clyde in Faslane 🏗️ were first sketched out back in 2023 📅 and they will upgrade facilities 🛠️ for the next generation of British submarines 🦈 as part of a whopping £15bn upgrade programme 💸 for the Royal Navy's shipyards that won't hit service until the early 2030s 🕒!! First Secretary of State Louise Haigh dropped her own hint on Sunday ☀️ that the government is commissioning that marine research vessel as part of this "new era of reindustrialisation" 🏭 with Healey set to unveil £115m in funding 💵 for the ship that will also sail into service in the early 2030s 🛥️ while he keeps repeating his thirsty line about backing British shipyards to boost national security 🛡️ and secure resilience in industries that drive growth today 🌱!!

Ahead of the big speech 🗣️ Healey said "By backing British shipyards we are not only boosting national security but also securing resilience in the industries that will drive growth today while building the capabilities the country needs for the future" 📈 which sounds like he's ready to rail the whole economy into shape 🍆 with some serious industrial action that Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith immediately called out as "reheated announcements" 🍲 with "no clarity on where the money is coming from" 💸!! Griffith added that Labour are running scared of making the tough choices needed to pay for Britain's defence 🛡️ and all they can offer is reannounced docks and more hot air 💨 from Healey while only the Conservatives will cut the welfare bill to fund defence 🏛️!! Charlotte Brumpton-Childs national secretary of the GMB union which has been campaigning hard for this move said it would be a "massive boost" for the UK's shipbuilding sector 🏗️ because for too long juicy contracts have been sent to overseas often subsidised yards overseas 🏭 and this policy could reinvigorate UK yards and the communities that depend on them like a proper industrial climax 💦!!

Prime Minister Andy Burnham who is due to drop his own big conference speech on Tuesday 🗣️ has previously spoken about his ambition to "reindustrialise" Britain including in talks last week with US President Donald Trump 🤝 but a fresh survey from the Confederation of British Industry is about to drop on Monday 📊 highlighting falling economic activity across key sectors such as retail 🛍️ and services in the three months to September with manufacturing declining more moderately 🏭!! CBI deputy chief economist Alpesh Paleja said rising energy and employment costs combined with weak demand were continuing to put pressure on profit margins 💰 and uncertainty ahead of next month's Budget is also holding back activity in some sectors while against the backdrop of renewed fiscal pressures the Budget must draw a clear red line under any more rises in the cost of hiring investing and doing business 📉!! The chancellor is also feeling heat from some of Labour's trade union backers to do more to tackle the cost of living 🔥 with Sharon Graham general secretary of the Unite union calling on Healey to "do something for workers and the working class" in his Budget by unfreezing income tax thresholds to put money back into people's pockets and taking further action on energy bills ⚡!!

In his conference speech Healey will also announce plans to bring back a training scheme run by trade unions to help workers in England gain new skills and adapt as technology including AI changes the workplace 🤖 with the Union Learning Fund getting £15m in taxpayers' money taken from existing government budgets 💵!! Employees do not need to be union members to benefit with support options ranging from essential English maths and digital skills to training for jobs in growing industries such as advanced manufacturing 🛠️ which is basically Healey's way of sliding into the DMs of the working class and promising them a proper skills upgrade so the whole reindustrialisation fantasy can finally get railed into reality 🍆 without anyone getting left behind in the dust of the old coal mines ⛏️!!
